{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{x},\,y(1)=2.
$$

Use the tangent line approximation of $y(x)$ at $x=1$ to approximate $y(1.5).$

feedback.problem:
Consider the initial value problem 

$$
{y}^{′}=x\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,y(3)=e.
$$

Use the tangent line approximation of $y(x)$ at $x=3$ to approximate $y(4).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $y(x)$ at the point $a=3$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =y(a)+{y}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =y(3)+{y}^{′}(3)(x-3).\end{aligned}
$$

From the initial condition, we know that $y(3)=e.$ We also know that ${y}^{′}(x)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡y,$ so

$$
{y}^{′}(3)=3\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)=3.
$$

Substituting our values for $y(3)$ and ${y}^{′}(3)$ into our expression for $L(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =y(3)+{y}^{′}(3)(x-3) \\  & =e+(3)(x-3) \\  & =3x+e-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can approximate $y(4)$ using $L(4).$ We get

$$
y(4)≈L(4)=3(4)+e-9=e+3
$$
